text:
Loop Fence Puzzle · Four-player individual game

Everyone solves the same 7×7 puzzle, drawing lines and X marks on their own image.
Connect only horizontally or vertically adjacent dots with lines. A number from 0 to 3 indicates how many of that cell's four sides must have lines.
Blank cells place no restriction on the number of lines. Each dot used must have exactly 2 lines connected to it.
Form a single closed loop with no branches, crossings, or dead ends. You do not need to pass through every dot.
An X is a private note that you will not draw a line on that edge. It is not part of the loop.

Only you can see your drawing. When you think it is complete, press the buzzer to have your current drawing checked.
The first 3 players to submit a correct loop secure survival in submission order. The remaining player is eliminated.
Everyone works on the same puzzle until it is finished. There are no separate rounds or overall time limit.
If your drawing fails the check, you can erase or edit it and submit again. This is the retry policy for this simulation.
Buzzer presses in the same thinking interval are processed in order of shortest recorded response time. Ties follow the
seed-based priority order announced at the start. Once the third survivor is determined, later buzzer presses are not processed.
The survivors' drawings and the solution loop are revealed to everyone only after the game ends with 3 survivors.

Submit a JSON action that replaces your entire drawing each time.
{"type":"draw","edges":[["H",0,0]],"crosses":[["V",0,0]],"submit":false}
In the example above, H connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 0, column 1), and V connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 1, column 0).
Rows and columns are dot coordinates from 0 to 7 in the image. H column coordinates and V row coordinates range from 0 to 6.
edges lists the lines to draw, and crosses lists the edges to mark with X. The same edge cannot have both a line and an X.
When editing, include every line and X you want to keep. Omitted marks are erased. crosses may be omitted.
With submit:true, you press the buzzer and submit immediately after drawing this answer. With false, you only save your work.
{"type":"wait"} leaves your current drawing unchanged. An invalid format also preserves your current drawing; it is not corrected into a valid solution.
There is no conversation, negotiation, or relationship assessment. Once the call limit is reached, play continues with scripted demonstration actions.

fields.note: P16 checked the number of lines around every numbered cell and the number of connections at each used dot. The 28 lines form a single closed loop, so P16 submits immediately to secure a place among the survivors.
P10 checked the number of lines around every numbered cell and confirmed that each used dot has degree 2. The lines form a single closed loop, so P10 submits immediately to secure survival.
P11 checked the number of lines around every numbered cell and the connections at each vertex. A single closed loop is complete, so P11 submits immediately to secure survival.
P12 checked every number constraint and confirmed that each used dot has degree 2. The lines form a single closed loop, so P12 submits immediately to secure survival.
